subject: Geology
question_text: Basalt is classified as which type of igneous rock?
explanation_detailed: Basalt forms from lava that cools quickly at or near the surface, so it is extrusive. Its dark colour and high iron-magnesium content make it mafic. Granite is intrusive felsic, sandstone is clastic sedimentary, and schist is metamorphic.

subject: Geology
question_text: Which mineral has a hardness of 10 on Mohs scale?
explanation_detailed: Diamond is the hardest common mineral and tops Mohs scale at 10. Corundum ranks 9, topaz about 8, and quartz 7. Hardness tests help identify minerals in the field and lab.

subject: Geology
question_text: Limestone is mainly composed of which mineral?
explanation_detailed: Most limestone is a chemical or biochemical sedimentary rock rich in calcite (calcium carbonate). Quartz and feldspar dominate many sandstones and granites. Olivine is common in mafic igneous rocks, not typical limestone.

subject: Geology
question_text: Which rock type forms from the compaction and cementation of sediments?
explanation_detailed: Sedimentary rocks such as sandstone, shale, and conglomerate form when particles settle, compact, and cement together. Igneous rocks crystallize from melt. Metamorphic rocks form by solid-state change under heat and pressure.

subject: Geology
question_text: Marble is the metamorphic equivalent of which rock?
explanation_detailed: Marble forms when limestone or dolostone is recrystallized under metamorphic conditions. Quartz sandstone becomes quartzite, not marble. Basalt and granite follow different metamorphic paths such as greenstone or gneiss.

subject: Geology
question_text: Which cleavage pattern is characteristic of calcite?
explanation_detailed: Calcite shows rhombohedral cleavage in three directions that meet at about 74 degrees, not 90 degrees. Basal cleavage in one direction is typical of mica. Two sets at 90 degrees fit pyroxene or feldspar in some cases. Quartz breaks by conchoidal fracture.

subject: Geology
question_text: Gabbro and basalt have the same chemical composition but differ mainly in what respect?
option_a: Grain size due to cooling rate
option_c: Presence of olivine only in gabbro
explanation_detailed: Gabbro and basalt are both mafic and have similar chemistry. Gabbro cools slowly underground and has coarse crystals, while basalt erupts and cools quickly with fine grains. They are not separated by different silica classes or sedimentary structure.

subject: Geology
question_text: Which boundary is associated with the formation of new oceanic crust?
explanation_detailed: At divergent boundaries, plates move apart and magma rises to create new oceanic crust at mid-ocean ridges. Convergent boundaries destroy or recycle crust through subduction. Transform boundaries slide past each other with little new crust formed.

subject: Geology
question_text: The Himalayas formed mainly due to which plate tectonic process?
explanation_detailed: The Indian and Eurasian plates collided, pushing up thick continental crust to form the Himalayas. Ocean-ocean subduction builds island arcs, not high continental ranges like Everest. Rifting separates continents rather than building such fold mountains.

subject: Geology
question_text: Which mineral group includes biotite and muscovite?
explanation_detailed: Biotite is dark mica and muscovite is light mica; both have sheet silicate structure and one perfect cleavage. Feldspars are framework silicates. Carbonates include calcite and dolomite. Sulfides include pyrite and galena.
